acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
acceptance.verdict: Guide-following output hits the structural must-haves the rubric actually checks for (nine-question dialogue before the body, metadata.yaml + evals/rubric.json scaffold, explicit Contract In/Out, honest flagging of the plugin.json/README/skill-eval steps left undone) while the isolated baseline — despite a competently written procedural body — never produces metadata.yaml, never touches evals/, and shows no sign of the nine-question groundwork at all.

checklist.note: body addresses the human author; no directive aimed at a reading agent
no code that sends repo/user/context data anywhere
no key, token, or credential embedded
destructive strings appear only as prose examples of what to look for; none executed
plain markdown throughout; nothing encoded or unreadable-on-purpose
no download-and-run or reach to an external host
no read of ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychain, cookies, or a token store
no sudo/setuid/persistence; no write outside the working tree
